newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks up across the board at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks up across the board at open.

text.p: The Australian share market opened higher on Thursday with stocks up across the board after the Dow set a new record high and base metal prices made a modest recovery on the London Metal Exchange.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 25.6 points higher at 2,340.2. The September share price index was up 13 points at 2,360 and at a 19.8 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said most factors were positive for the market and traders were excited by the prospect that the All Ordinaries index could set a new record high later in the session.
"The market has had a pretty good run lately, but I wouldn't discount the possibility of it reaching a new high today," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney brokerage, Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said the market was nearing a point where profit takers were likely to enter but that he didn't expect the likely pull-back to be too severe.

Driving the market's early rises were strong performances from the major banks, particularly ANZ and Westpac. Bellwether issue BHP was also underpinning gains and was the most active stock in early trade.
Transport issues Mayne Nickless and Brambles continued to climb in the wake of the high bid for TNT by Dutch telcoms and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
